rationale: A wins because it keeps the sharp edges without overstating the record. Its line that "The unnamed supply source is a gap a competitor reporter will probe" is exactly the adult supervision this story needs. B has stronger headline energy, but "branded drugmakers want it stopped" and "Hims & Hers is scaling them anyway" go past the supplied facts; that is how a decent angle becomes a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: "A newly profitable Hims & Hers bets its margins on compounded weight-loss drugs" overreaches slightly; the update says recently profitable, not that margins are materially exposed.
It misses a viable consumer-health access angle: cheaper compounded GLP-1s plus FDA-flagged risk is not the same as the refused "Why patients are choosing" hallucination.
"Decay: 4hr" on the FDA angle is too theatrical for a fact block that gives no date or concrete FDA action.
gaps_in_B: "branded drugmakers want it stopped" is stronger than "pushed back" and invents intent or requested remedy.
"Hims & Hers is scaling them anyway" overstates the fact pattern; the update says launching access, not scaling.
"whether the model is allowed to exist" turns an FDA risk flag into a legal-existence question without enough evidence.
"Patients priced out of branded weight-loss drugs" may be true in the market, but it is not in the supplied update; the safer angle is affordability trade-off, not a claimed patient condition.
